newsitem.title: UK: Large explosion heard in Belfast amid unrest.
newsitem.headline: Large explosion heard in Belfast amid unrest.

text.p: A large explosion was heard in central Belfast early on Monday amid Catholic violence to protest against the holding of a Protestant Orange Order parade on Sunday.
Residents said the blast was heard, apparently from the northwest part of the Northern Ireland capital. Police said they had no details of any explosion but were checking.
The explosion echoed around the city centre shortly after midnight amid violent scenes in Catholic Irish nationalist parts of the city over the holding of the parade.

Cars were hijacked and set on fire and the Irish Republican Army claimed responsibility in a statement to a news organisation for the shooting on Sunday of a policewoman in a police vehicle. She was hospitalised with facial injuries.
The IRA, which enjoys support among some section of the 40 per cent Catholic minority, is fighting a 28-year war to end British rule of Northern Ireland.
